The ANALYZER's rows for `extends-probe-roles.icl`. The file itself exists for the `extends` RULING PROBE — `extends-probe-roles.probe.json` pins the census's slot ROLES per declaration, checked by `extends-probe-roles-check.mts`. These rows are here so `runLang("clean")` exercises the same file through the analyzer too, and so the two suites cannot drift apart.

The one defect class this file pins is a SPELLING mismatch, and it is worth stating precisely because it is invisible to every count-based check on this lane. An operator IS a class name in Clean, and the two sites spell it differently: a DECLARATION writes `class (>>=) a where` and an INSTANCE writes `instance >>= Thing where`. The analyzer read the declaration's `name` field verbatim as `(>>=)` and the instance's as `>>=`, so before the fix `declaredTypeNames` held `(>>=)` while both lookups held `>>=` and BOTH missed: `implements` reported `isExternalClass: true` for a class declared in the same file, and `overrides` refused the edge because the in-file member set was unreachable. Measured on the 312-file corpus: 24 `implements` edges carried the false `isExternalClass`, and the false count is now 0. No edge was ADDED or REMOVED by the fix on that corpus — the corpus spells its operator-named classes on one line (`class (==) … ::`, clean-stdlib/StdOverloaded.icl:23), which gives the member set nothing to read — so the `overrides` half is pinned HERE, where a `where` block gives it something to read, because otherwise the correction would ship untested.

expectSymbols.comment: an operator-named class publishes with its DECLARATION's spelling, parentheses included

expectSymbols.name: Box
expectSymbols.comment: a class with a kind annotation and two members
the SAME operator-named class in the `where` form, so its member set is readable
memberDeclaredName unparenthesises, so the member is `>>=` while its owner keeps the declared spelling

expectRelationships.comment: THE FIX, half one: `class (==)` is declared in THIS file at line 47, so `isExternalClass` must be false. It read true before the fix because the declaration publishes `(==)` and the instance reads `==`.
the same correction on the `where`-form class

THE FIX, half two: the in-file guard could not see `(>>=)`'s member set under the key `>>=`, so this edge was refused for a class this file declares. Endpoints are qualified on both sides and the direction is instance-member -> class-member, unchanged by the fix.
the ordinary, non-operator case, which must be unaffected by the fix
a unit-annotated instance target still publishes its member and still overrides
an instance target that is a TYPE EXPRESSION (`()`) publishes a symbol by that text — known limit 12 in the analyzer doc, pinned here so a change to it is visible
the negative half of the flag: `Eq` is NOT declared here, so `isExternalClass` stays true. Without this row the fix could pass by making the flag always false.

a `derive` declaration is an instance too, and it carries NO `isExternalClass` key at all — the derive branch does not set it. Pinned by omission rather than by value, because `meta.isExternalClass: null` would also be satisfied by a key holding `null`, and the honest statement is that the field is absent.

the class context, published as `references` and NOT as `extends`. This is the label the construct earns, and the row that would change first if anyone relabelled it — see the `extends` forbids below.
the operator-named constraint on an INSTANCE, same label

forbidRelationships.comment: `extends` is RULED at 0 on this lane (script/m14/clean-ruled.ts, instrument B position census: 0 UNCLASSIFIED of 5,567 declarations). No edge of that type may appear here, and this row is what convicts a future edit that relabels a dictionary requirement as a supertype — `| Eq a` on line 65 and `| == e` on line 91 are the two sites in this file where that mistake would be easiest to make.

the class endpoint uses the BARE spelling. The class member's identity comes from the member set, which is keyed by the declaration, so a parenthesised endpoint here would be a different symbol and would not resolve — pinning the exact spelling so a 'normalisation' that changes it is caught.

no SELF-edge. A polymorphic instance publishes no symbol of its own, so its members are attributed to the class and the two endpoints compose to the same string; the analyzer refuses those (mutant clean/overrides-self-edge-guard-dropped).
the direction is instance-member -> class-member and never the reverse: a class member is abstract and overrides nothing.
endpoints are QUALIFIED. A bare member name collides with every other member of that name in any consumer.

the exact defect this fixture exists to catch, stated as a FORBID: `Eq` is not declared in this file, so its `isExternalClass` must never read false. Without this row the two halves of the fix could both pass by making the flag constant.
